summary: The sample implements the requested Node.js + Mongoose immutable ledger, transactionality and idempotency and was exercised against the provided cluster. Core functional requirements are met (models, transactions-with-sessions, unique transactionRef, idempotent seed, singleton connection). Findings: numeric-money fields use JavaScript Number (risk of rounding); no automated retry logic for transient transaction errors; no unit tests or CI mocks; no monitoring/metrics instrumentation; package.json uses a permissive range for mongoose (package-lock.json present). Several discovered best practices are present and discoverable via the installed skills and Microsoft Learn; a few best-practices remain only in prior knowledge or are not documented well enough for an agent and are listed as documentation gaps below.

requirement_results.requirement: The ledger is a Node.js application that uses Mongoose as its ODM: accounts and transactions are defined as Mongoose schemas and models, and every read and write of ledger data goes through them.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/models/account.js (lines 3-8), app/src/models/transaction.js (lines 3-9), app/src/transactions.js (lines 1-3, 20-28)

requirement_results.requirement: Every debit and every credit is recorded as its own transaction document in Azure DocumentDB, inserted once and left unchanged afterwards (no code path updates or deletes a posted transaction document).
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/transactions.js (lines 19-21 insert transaction); no code path performs updates/deletes against Transaction documents elsewhere in repo

requirement_results.requirement: Each account has a balance snapshot document that holds its current balance (e.g. an Account model with a balance field).
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/models/account.js (line 6: balance field)

requirement_results.requirement: Posting a transaction runs inside an Azure DocumentDB multi-document transaction: a Mongoose session (withTransaction, or start/commit/abort) wraps both the insert of the transaction document and the update of the account balance snapshot, so both are committed together or neither is.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/transactions.js (lines 15-31 uses session.withTransaction and passes session to save and findOneAndUpdate)

requirement_results.requirement: The balance snapshot is adjusted by the posted amount in the direction of the entry (a credit raises it, a debit lowers it).
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/transactions.js (line 13 computes signedAmount; line 26 uses $inc with signedAmount)

requirement_results.requirement: Every transaction document carries a transactionRef field supplied with the posting request.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/models/transaction.js (line 4: transactionRef required:true) and app/src/transactions.js (line 20 constructs Transaction with transactionRef)

requirement_results.requirement: The transactionRef field has a unique index, declared in the Mongoose schema or created in code, so Azure DocumentDB enforces uniqueness.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/models/transaction.js (lines 11-13 declare unique index on transactionRef)

requirement_results.requirement: A second posting with an already-used transactionRef is rejected: the unique index makes the insert fail and the enclosing transaction aborts, so the balance snapshot is not changed by the duplicate.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/transactions.js (lines 32-41 catch duplicate-key code 11000 and return existing transaction/account), demo script shows duplicate attempt handled (app/src/demo.js lines 17-26), and verification ran the demo successfully per builder_report.

doc_gaps.topic: Public pattern for Mongoose transactions + session usage
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A concise, public example on Microsoft Learn that demonstrates the exact Mongoose pattern: startSession(), session.withTransaction(async callback), and the need to pass { session } to every Model operation inside the callback, plus correct endSession() placement and error-label handling for retries.
doc_gaps.where_searched: documentdb quickstarts and installed documentdb-* skills; searches for 'Mongoose withTransaction example' returned tutorial text but no small copy-paste snippet that shows retry labels and session passing in one place.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The builder implemented the pattern correctly, but an agent searching for a single authoritative snippet might not have found it quickly (P02 was prior_knowledge_only).
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A short 'Transactions with Mongoose on Azure DocumentDB' page: 1) sample code showing startSession()/withTransaction(), 2) explicit passing of { session } to every Model method, 3) example finally block with session.endSession(), 4) guidance on handling TransientTransactionError and UnknownTransactionCommitResult labels with a bounded retry/backoff loop.

doc_gaps.topic: Guidance on audit fields for ledger transactions
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A concise public recommendation listing recommended immutable audit fields for ledger transactions (createdAt, createdBy, transactionRef, source, idempotency metadata) and an example schema.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Microsoft Learn and the documentdb-data-modeling skill; searches for 'audit metadata ledger DocumentDB' returned no single authoritative page.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The sample included basic audit fields (transactionRef, createdAt, metadata) but omitted createdBy; an agent might decide different fields based on prior knowledge and produce inconsistent schemas.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A 'Ledger design patterns' subsection listing recommended immutable audit fields, example Mongoose schema, and notes on what to store in 'metadata' versus explicit fields.

doc_gaps.topic: Explicit note: avoid TTL on transaction/ledger collections
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: No Microsoft Learn page explicitly states 'do not use TTL indexes for immutable ledger collections' (this is currently only in prior knowledge conversations).
doc_gaps.where_searched: Microsoft Learn and skill docs, queries searching for TTL + ledger guidance.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: No TTL index present in this sample. However, absent explicit guidance an agent might accidentally add a TTL index to a ledger.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a small paragraph on the data-modeling page: 'Ledger collections should not use TTL indexes; store expirable data in separate collections.'

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A single short note in the quickstart that recommends exact pinning semantics for sample repositories (for Node: pin exact version in package.json or commit package-lock.json and recommend `npm ci`).
doc_gaps.where_searched: Quickstart and tutorial pages: they describe tested driver versions but do not prescribe sample repo pinning policy.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Builder initially attempted to pin an exact version, hit a registry mismatch, and used a caret range. This left the repo with a range rather than an explicit pinned package.json entry.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a 'Pin dependencies' short guidance paragraph in the Node quickstart: preferred sample repository pattern (exact pins in package.json OR commit package-lock.json and instruct `npm ci`).

doc_gaps.topic: Agent-facing decision guidance for API surface
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: There is no explicit guidance in the skills/quickstarts telling an agent whether to prefer CLI-only samples vs REST+CLI in small demos.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Skill docs and quickstarts; this decision is currently left to the builder as model_default.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Builder selected REST+CLI by default (reasonable), but agents may make inconsistent surface choices for similar samples.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add an agent-kit rule: 'For service quickstart samples that demonstrate read/write flows, prefer a minimal REST surface plus a CLI seed/demo script unless user explicitly asks for CLI-only.'

doc_gaps.topic: Public snippet for transaction retry semantics
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A small public example showing how to detect retryable transaction errors (TransientTransactionError, UnknownTransactionCommitResult) and perform bounded exponential-backoff retries in Node/Mongoose against Azure DocumentDB.
doc_gaps.where_searched: documentdb-connection and quickstart docs; pieces exist but not a compact, copy-paste retry wrapper.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The sample does not implement a retry wrapper; having the snippet would make it straightforward to add and would reduce the risk of incorrect retry implementations.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A small retry helper in the Node quickstart showing error-label checks, backoff, and max-attempts, plus tests that simulate transient errors.

doc_gaps.topic: Entra ID example for Mongoose drivers
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A short Node snippet showing how to wire DefaultAzureCredential into the MongoDB driver's OIDC callback for a cluster that has MicrosoftEntraID auth enabled.
doc_gaps.where_searched: documentdb security docs and quickstarts; docs mention it but lack a short copy-paste example.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Sample defaults to SCRAM and documents Entra ID as an option. A short example would help teams adopt Entra ID securely.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A 10-line code example demonstrating the driver's token refresh callback and using @azure/identity DefaultAzureCredential to obtain tokens for the MongoDB driver.
